title: Three letters that know where you are going
text: {{1}} commercial airport answers to a three-letter code, and {{2}} a few exceptions the system took shape in the 1930s, {{3}} airlines needed short labels for telex messages. Some codes are straightforward; others are inherited {{4}} the weather stations and airfields of an earlier age. Chicago's O'Hare is ORD, {{5}} recalls Orchard Field, the site's original name, and New Orleans is MSY, {{6}} letters honour the aviator John Moisant. {{7}} same logic gave Canada its Y-prefixes, from YVR in Vancouver to YYZ in Toronto. {{8}} some codes are instantly readable, others are pure archaeology, and decoding them is a small pleasure hidden in every itinerary.

gaps.explanation: 'Every' + singular noun for the whole set.
'With a few exceptions' is the fixed phrase.
